questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Uganda about 241,038 square kilometres; Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Djibouti about 23,200 square kilometres; Mauritius about 2,040 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Uganda?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city is Kampala.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Uganda?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Uganda on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: It shares land borders with five countries including the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west, Kenya to the east, South Sudan to the north, Rwanda to the south-west, and Tanzania to the south.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Uganda on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Uganda on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Kampala?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Uganda is Kampala.
